h1: The 8 Best Laptop Charging Carts for Classrooms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Classroom Charging Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight laptop charging carts for classrooms, from 16 to 32 devices, compared on locks, ventilation, power protection and price.
summary: The Meteteel 20 is the best classroom charging cart, a 95% pre-assembled steel cart with locks on both sides. The VEVOR is the pick for security, the POCHAR 30 for big rosters, and the Plugsharge for the highest capacity at 32 devices. The Kraftgen is the only open cart and the cheapest.
intro: A charging cart fails in a classroom for boring reasons: a roster that outgrew the bays, a lock that secures only one side, or a power strip that trips when twenty devices draw current at once. Capacity and security get the headlines, but power protection and slot size decide whether the cart still works in October, after the cases and chargers have changed.

We reviewed eight carts from 16 to 32 devices and ranked them on the spec sheets: capacity, locking, device size limits, ventilation and electrical protection. Where the listing does not state something, such as a weight rating or a lock, we say so and do not guess. A cart bought to the wrong slot size is the costliest mistake here, because the whole fleet has to fit.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: A 20-device cart that is ready for day-one handout.
products.description:
The Meteteel 20 holds 20 devices, arrives 95% pre-assembled and has independent front and back locks. The steel frame is ventilated for all-day charging. Independent locks matter because a single-sided lock leaves the cable side open to anyone who walks around the cart, a gap that mostly shows up after dismissal.

It leads because 20 slots fit the common 18 to 22 student room and almost no building is left. Against the 18-device Meteteel, you get two more slots at the same $200 to $500 bracket. The VEVOR adds surge protection and a lock and key, but holds four fewer devices.

Buy it for a standard class that wants a cart ready on day one. The caveat is the listing: slot dimensions are not stated, so confirm thickness for chunky cases before you order.

products.name: VEVOR 16 Device Charging Station with Lock & Key, Mobile Charging Cart
products.verdict: A locked 16-device cart with built-in surge protection.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 16 devices up to 15.6 inch screens, with a lock and key, built-in surge protection, an integrated power strip and two locking casters. Surge protection matters on a cart because a single spike on the building circuit can take out an entire row of chargers, and thus the batteries behind them.

It ranks second because capacity is lower: four fewer devices than the Meteteel 20. In exchange it fits larger 15.6 inch laptops, which the Meteteel 18 and both POCHAR carts cap at 14 inches. The lock and key is the other differentiator for rooms that stay open between periods.

Buy it for a small class or rooms where the cart sits unattended. The caveat is the 16 slot ceiling, and the listing does not describe assembly, so budget time for setup.

products.name: POCHAR 30 Devices 14'' Screen Laptop Charging Cart for K-12 Classrooms
products.verdict: A 30-device cart with circuit breaker and grounding protection.
products.description:
The POCHAR 30 holds 30 devices with screens up to 14 inches and an open-back cooling design, a circuit breaker with grounding protection and two locking casters. The circuit breaker is the key spec. At 30 devices, simultaneous charging draws serious current, and a breaker trips instead of letting wiring overheat.

It ranks third because it ships flat-packed, so assembly takes real time, unlike the pre-assembled Meteteel. In return it gives you 30 slots and electrical protection, and it undercuts the Plugsharge's 32 slots with a lock-friendly layout. The open back helps airflow around chargers.

Buy it for large classes or two sections sharing one cart. The caveat is the 14 inch cap, which excludes 15.6 inch laptops, and the work of putting it together.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 18 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: An 18-device cart that draws from a single wall outlet.
products.description:
This Meteteel takes 18 devices in slots capped at 14 inch screens and 1.4 inches of thickness. It draws from a single wall outlet and uses zig-zag cable dividers with star-pattern ventilation. The single outlet draw is its practical strength: older buildings with few outlets can still power it.

It sits fourth because the 20-device sibling offers more slots in the same $200 to $500 bracket, which makes this model hard to justify unless the roster is exactly 18. The thickness limit is also stricter than the POCHAR mixed-fleet cart's 1.5 inches.

Buy it for rosters near 18 in an older classroom. The caveat is device thickness: a laptop in a padded sleeve can exceed 1.4 inches and simply will not slide into the slot.

products.name: Plugsharge 32-Device Laptop Charging Cart for Chromebooks, iPad & Tablets
products.verdict: The highest-capacity cart here at 32 devices.
products.description:
The Plugsharge holds 32 devices up to 15.6 inch screens, with surge and ground fault protection, 32 individual cable organizers and numbered slots on an open rack. Numbered slots matter in shared use because they assign every device to a bay, so a missing laptop shows up at once during check-in.

It ranks fifth because the open rack is less secure than the locked carts above, and the listing mentions no lock. It wins on capacity and screen size, matching the 15.6 inch limit of the VEVOR with double the bays. For a locked alternative with 30 bays, look at the POCHAR.

Buy it for oversized rosters or two classes sharing a cart. The caveat is security: you need your own lockable cabinet or room plan, since the cart will not protect the devices overnight.

products.name: POCHAR 30 Unit Device Charging Station for Chromebook, iPad, 14'' Laptop
products.verdict: A locked 30-bay cart rated for mixed devices.
products.description:
This POCHAR fits 30 devices up to 14 inch screens and 1.5 inches deep, rated for a mixed fleet. It has numbered bays, removable doors and four keys total, two per lock. The mixed-fleet rating matters because Chromebooks, iPads and laptops differ in thickness and charger placement, and a cart built only for laptops wastes bays.

It ranks sixth because it lists no electrical protection, unlike the 30-device POCHAR above, which includes a circuit breaker and grounding. That omission is notable at 30 chargers. The locks and mixed-fleet design are its pitch, and the removable doors ease access during class.

Buy it for classrooms that mix Chromebooks, iPads and laptops. The caveat is power: confirm protection on the live listing, or put the cart on a protected circuit.
products.idealFor: Mixed Chromebook, iPad and laptop fleets.

products.name: ALT Technology 30-Bay Mobile School Charging Cart Station for Chromebook, Tablet
products.verdict: A 32-device cart with UL-approved power strips.
products.description:
The ALT cart holds 32 devices across two shelves, with a separate cable shelf, UL-approved power strips and slots of 1 by 14 by 10.5 inches for laptops up to 14 inches. UL approval on the strips means a recognized safety standard covers the part that carries the current, which many carts do not state.

It ranks seventh because the title says 30 bays while the listing states 32, a mismatch you need to resolve before buying. Its 1 inch slot is also the narrowest stated in the group, tighter than the Meteteel 18's 1.4 inches, so cases are a real risk.

Buy it if you are comparing 30-bay carts and value stated slot dimensions and certified strips. The caveat is thickness: measure every device with its case, because a 1 inch slot rules out many protective sleeves.

products.name: Kraftgen 16-Bay Open Charging Cart for Chromebooks, Laptops, Tablets & iPads
products.verdict: A lower-cost open cart for fast daily access.
products.description:
The Kraftgen holds 16 devices in an open design with UL-listed power strips, 3 inch non-marring casters, removable dividers, padded shelves and rear cable clips. It is the only cart here with no lock, and the only one in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks last because open design means no lockup, which suits only supervised rooms. Padded shelves and non-marring casters protect devices and floors, but they do not replace security. Next to the VEVOR, which has the same 16 slots, you save a bracket and give up the lock and surge protection.

Buy it for classrooms that value fast daily access and have a secure room. The caveat is simple: do not leave it unattended, since nothing here stops a walk-off.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is how many devices the cart holds. Match it to your largest class and add a few spare slots for growth and repairs. Options here run from 16 to 32. The ALT listing shows a title and spec mismatch on bay count, so check the number in the bullets, not just the title, and count the bays against the devices you actually own.

Locks keep devices safe overnight. Independent front and back locks, as on the Meteteel 20, secure both the door and the cable side. The POCHAR mixed-fleet cart ships two locks and four keys. Look for lock and key in the bullets, and note that the Plugsharge and Kraftgen list none, which pushes security onto the room.

Charging dozens of devices draws heavy current. Surge protection, a circuit breaker or UL-listed strips reduce the risk of tripped circuits and damage. The POCHAR 30 lists a breaker with grounding, and the Plugsharge adds ground fault protection. Check what the listing names, and ask your facilities team about the circuit.

Each slot caps screen size and thickness, such as 14 inches and 1.4 inches on the Meteteel 18. A device in a padded case may not fit. Measure your thickest device with its case, then compare with the slot size, because a cart that rejects a few devices is a failed purchase. The ALT cart states a 1 inch slot, the narrowest here.

Pre-assembled carts arrive ready, while flat-pack carts need hours of building. The Meteteel 20 is 95% assembled, and the POCHAR ships flat. For a rollout before the school year, assembly time matters. Check the listing for the assembly percent or a build time, and plan staff time for flat-pack carts so the fleet is in service on the first day.

faq.q: How many devices should a cart hold?
faq.a: Match your largest class plus a few spare slots. Carts here run from 16, like the VEVOR, to 32, like the Plugsharge. Rosters that grow mid-year are the reason to buy more capacity than today needs, since a full cart has no room for loaners.
Ignoring slot thickness. The Meteteel 18 limits devices to 1.4 inches, and the ALT cart lists a 1 inch slot. A laptop in a thick case will not fit, so measure it first, case included.

faq.q: Is a locked cart worth it?
faq.a: For unattended rooms, yes. The VEVOR and Meteteel 20 are the locked picks, with a lock and key and independent front and back locks. The Kraftgen is open, so it needs a supervised room.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: The Meteteel 20 is 95% pre-assembled, so setup is mostly rolling it into place and plugging in. The POCHAR carts ship flat-packed and need building. Follow the maker's manual and tighten all hardware.

faq.q: How do I keep it running?
faq.a: Keep the vents clear and the cables organized so heat does not build. Numbered slots and cable organizers, like on the Plugsharge, make it easier to spot a loose charger. Check the strips after any breaker trip and replace worn cables promptly.

faq.q: Can I mix Chromebooks and iPads?
faq.a: The POCHAR 30 Unit is rated for a mixed fleet of Chromebooks, iPads and 14 inch laptops, up to 1.5 inches thick. For other carts, confirm tablet and Chromebook support on the live listing, including the slot depth.

finalTake: Buy the Meteteel 20 for a typical classroom of 18 to 22 students. Rooms that sit unattended should choose the locked VEVOR, large rosters the POCHAR with its circuit breaker, and shared fleets the Plugsharge. Measure your thickest device in its case before ordering, since slot limits are the most common reason a cart does not fit.
